gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch correctly addresses the stated issue: it moves all pkg/ packages to internal/, extracts a shared runner package from duplicated concurrency code in install/check/update commands, creates internal/helpers/path with the ExpandTilda helper, adds HasReleaseBlock() to the Package interface, updates all imports throughout cmd/ and internal/, and renames the package declarations from 'config' to 'pkg'. The patch is comprehensive and well-structured.
base_vs_gold_expectation: The base state will definitely fail: the test patch moves test files to internal/ paths and updates imports to github.com/babarot/afx/internal/..., but in the base state no internal/ source packages exist. The go test compilation will fail for every package. The gold patch creates all required internal/ source packages, so tests pass after patching.
too_narrow_risks: No tests for the internal/runner package (runner.go, progress.go) despite it being a key requirement in the issue ('factored out into an internal runner package'). The Execute function, NewProgress with []string, and the Package/TaskFunc/Result types are all untested.

The test patch actually removes TestCountRemaining and TestNewProgress from config_test.go but never re-adds equivalent tests for the runner package. These functions moved to internal/runner/progress.go but have no test coverage.

An alternative solution that simply moves pkg/ to internal/ without creating the runner package (keeping inline concurrency in cmd files) would pass all tests, since no test verifies the runner package exists or is used.
No explicit verification that old pkg/ import paths are no longer used anywhere in production code. A solution could leave stale pkg/ files and still pass.
No go build ./... or go vet ./... step — compilation is only checked for packages that have test files.
too_broad_risks: Tests cover a large number of packages (26 test files across 17 directories) which increases the surface for unrelated failures, though each is directly relevant to the migration task.
implementation_coupling: Tests are tightly coupled to the exact package path 'github.com/babarot/afx/internal/pkg' — an alternative name like 'internal/config' would fail. However, this path is explicitly specified in the issue requirements, so this coupling is justified.
The test patch uses the specific import alias 'afxpkg' matching the gold patch exactly, though Go allows any alias.
cmd/meta_test.go references specific type names (afxpkg.Package, afxpkg.GitHub, afxpkg.Config, afxpkg.Main, afxpkg.Gist) which must match the gold patch's package naming.
environment_risks: go 1.25.0 is specified in go.mod — the Docker image must have this Go version available or the build will fail regardless of the solution.
The test runner uses -json flag and PIPESTATUS which requires bash; eval.sh uses bash explicitly so this should be fine.
Some tests (github_test.go, update_test.go) use httpmock which starts local HTTP servers — these could be fragile but are from the base test suite and pre-existing.
mismatches: The issue explicitly requires the runner factoring ('The duplicated concurrent execution/progress handling in install and check should be factored out into an internal runner package'), but the tests have zero coverage for the runner package, creating a gap between issue requirements and test verification.

The issue mentions 'afx check' and 'afx install' should 'still support cancellation via context and preserve the previous concurrency limit/progress behavior' — none of this behavioral preservation is tested.

evidence.detail: RUNNABLE_TEST_FILES list contains no internal/runner test files. grep for 'runner' in eval.sh returns zero matches.
Test patch removes TestCountRemaining and TestNewProgress from config_test.go (lines 328-435 of the embedded patch) without adding runner package tests.
Gold patch creates internal/runner/runner.go (79 lines) and internal/runner/progress.go (renamed from pkg/config/status.go) — both completely untested.
Lines 9-10 explicitly require: 'The duplicated concurrent execution/progress handling in install and check should be factored out into an internal runner package used by both commands.'
Base state confirms pkg/ structure exists; internal/ directory does not exist, confirming base will fail the tests.

summary: The gold patch correctly implements the pkg-to-internal migration including a new runner package. The tests adequately verify the package migration by checking compilation and functionality of all moved packages. However, the tests have a significant gap: no coverage for the internal/runner package, which is a key requirement (concurrent execution factoring). A solution that merely moves pkg/ to internal/ without extracting the runner would pass all tests. The test patch also removes runner-related tests (TestCountRemaining, TestNewProgress) without replacement. Recommend adding runner package tests and optionally a go build ./... check.
